- Estimated steady-state monthly tokens: ~500M tokens (combined input+output). You called out ~100M input / ~400M output as a starting point — please confirm below.
- Peak concurrency: ~20-30 concurrent requests at peak.
- Target budget range: you mentioned wanting to stay within ~$10k–$25k / month; you also said target unit economics of roughly $15–$25 / 1M tokens as a north star.

Open asks (can you confirm these?):
1) Finalized monthly token split (input vs output) and any expected growth rate over the next 6 months. I attached the quick MAU/token spreadsheet we walked through (mau_estimates.csv).
2) Which flows are strictly latency-critical (p95 target <= 300ms) vs which can tolerate 500-1000ms?
3) Any compliance requirements (SOC2 / VPC / data residency) that would push you toward Private/Dedicated options?

What I’m going to prepare
- A short pricing table with unit economics for three recommended options: Hosted standard (cost-optimized), Hosted low-latency (streaming/low-p95), and Dedicated (reserved capacity + SLA).
- Concrete numbers showing cost per 1M tokens and expected monthly cost given your estimates. I’ll include how batching and streaming affect both cost and perceived latency.

Next steps
- Can you confirm the numbers above today/tomorrow? If yes, I’ll set up a 45-min technical deep dive with Vivek and Dev to lock in config (batch targets, preferred model variants, and rollout plan).

- Peak concurrency: 25 concurrent requests for the payment path, bursts up to ~40 for promotional traffic.

Alex — great, thanks for confirming. Below is a concise pricing & trade-off summary so you have something to review before the technical sync. I attached a one-page SLA/pricing stub (SLA_pricing_table.pdf) as well.

Summary (ballpark numbers for your 500M tokens/mo baseline)
- Option A — Hosted (cost-optimized)
  - Unit: ~$12 / 1M tokens
  - Expected monthly: ~ $6,000 (500M tokens)
  - Latency: p95 ~ 600-900ms (depends on batching). Good for non-critical personalization flows.
  - When to pick: If budget is primary constraint and only subset of flows require low p95.

- Option B — Hosted Low-Latency (streaming-enabled)
  - Unit: ~$35 / 1M tokens (premium for reserved low-p95 instances and streaming paths)
  - Expected monthly: ~ $17,500 (500M tokens)
  - Latency: p95 ~ 150-350ms with streaming + small batch windows
  - Notes: Streaming reduces perceived latency but can increase output token overhead by ~5-10% (more assistant tokens emitted incrementally).

- Option C — Dedicated (reserved capacity)
  - Unit (reserved): ~$22 / 1M tokens (committed capacity discounts available at 12mo)
  - Expected monthly: ~ $11,000 (500M tokens)
  - Latency: p95 ~ 120-300ms depending on instance sizing and model choice
  - When to pick: you want predictable capacity, better p95 at a lower long-run cost vs hosted low-latency, and enterprise controls (VPC, KMS).

Batching vs streaming trade-off (quick heuristics)
- Batching (larger batch sizes) reduces per-token cost by sharing compute across requests but increases tail latency for individual requests. Typical cost wins at 2-4x batching for the payment workload, but only if you can tolerate an extra 50-200ms latency.
- Streaming reduces time-to-first-token and perceived latency for users but can increase token counts slightly and adds complexity to the client integration. Good for sub-300ms p95 targets when combined with small batch windows.

SLO-driven pricing model idea
- We can offer an SLO tiering approach on top of the unit price: base unit price for best-effort (hosted) and a premium for a guaranteed p95 bucket (<300ms). This maps to either reserved low-latency capacity (dedicated) or a higher-priced hosted low-latency tier.

Proposed immediate next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (45 min) — recommend: Vivek + Dev + Alex + Priya. Purpose: pick model variant, target batch sizes, and confirm QPS/throughput assumptions so we can firm up a proposal.
2) After technical sync: I’ll share a formal quote and a 30-day pilot plan (we can do a small reserved pool + overflow to hosted).

If that looks good, I’ll send a calendar invite for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks —
